rows.label: Save the Children UK group total expenditure, year to 31 December 2025 (pounds)

source.title: Save the Children UK, Annual Report and Financial Statements 2025

rows.explainer: Charitable activities £233.6m, raising funds £39.7m (donations and legacies £29.4m, shops £10.2m) and other expenditure £2.5m (a sub-let floor of the head office). Read by both of charityevals' Save the Children models for the overhead multiplier.

rows.label: Save the Children UK expenditure on charitable activities, 2025 (pounds)

source.title: Save the Children UK, Annual Report and Financial Statements 2025

rows.explainer: Nutrition, livelihoods, health, protection and rights, education, rapid-onset emergencies and advocacy and awareness, each with its share of management, administration and programme support costs (including the core contributions to Save the Children International). Read by both Save the Children models.

rows.label: Save the Children UK staff costs, 2025 (pounds)

source.title: Save the Children UK, Annual Report and Financial Statements 2025

rows.explainer: Wages £43.8m, National Insurance £5.2m, pensions £2.9m and other staff costs £3.8m: £55.7m for 863 full-time equivalents. Country staff abroad are employed by Save the Children International and paid from the grants to it, so they are not in this figure. Read by both Save the Children models for the staff share of cost.

rows.label: Consumption per person of the UK families Save the Children's work reaches, as a share of UK consumption per person
rows.explainer: Our judgment, read by both Save the Children models (the two-child limit's families in the advocacy model, the families in crisis the UK programmes reach): families on Universal Credit with several children are mostly in the bottom fifth of incomes, and their spending per person is lower still because the household is large (equivalence scales give a child about a third of an adult's need). National-accounts consumption per person (facts/united_kingdom.json) runs above survey spending, so the share is of that figure: 40% (25-60%).

rows.label: Elrha (humanitarian research and innovation) restricted expenditure, 2025 (pounds)

source.title: Save the Children UK, Annual Report and Financial Statements 2025

rows.explainer: Spending of Elrha, Save the Children UK's subsidiary charity that funds humanitarian research (Research for Health in Humanitarian Crises) and the Humanitarian Innovation Fund. The accounts book it inside the thematic lines without saying which; we take it out of the rapid-onset emergencies line (it funds research on crises) and model it with advocacy as research. Read by both Save the Children models, so the two split the spending in full.
